---
title: "2,3-DPG and pH in stored RBC"
subtitle: "Reproducible analysis — *Cells* submission"
author:
  - name: Juan Sahuquillo
  - name: Marta Peris
date: "2026-02-02"
date-modified: "2026-11-1"
abstract: |
  Red blood cell (RBC) transfusion aims to restore tissue oxygen delivery, yet a stored unit's capacity to unload oxygen depends on 2,3-diphosphoglycerate (2,3-DPG), the principal allosteric modulator of hemoglobin–oxygen affinity. Randomized trials comparing fresher with older units have been consistently null, and all have used storage duration as the exposure variable. We asked whether storage age reflects the metabolic state of individual units. Twenty-four leukodepleted packed RBC units were sampled serially from day 3 to day 42 of standard cold storage. 2,3-DPG was quantified by liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS) with isotopically labelled internal standards, pH was measured in parallel, and trajectories were modelled by linear mixed effects with unit-level random intercepts. At day 3, 2,3-DPG spanned a twenty-fold range across units of identical age (0.8–14.7 µmol/g Hb; median 4.8): some were already near-depleted at the earliest sampled timepoint, while others retained near-physiological concentrations. This heterogeneity collapsed rapidly - median values fell to 27% of day-3 levels by day 7 and by more than 90% by day 14 (β = −0.298 µmol/g Hb per day, p < 0.001) - and were below the limit of detection in most units after day 17. pH declined monotonically to 6.40 ± 0.04 by day 42 (β = −0.0163 units per day, p < 0.001). Units of identical storage age therefore differ markedly in the levels of the me-tabolite that governs oxygen unloading, and are depleted long before the 42-day expiry limit, suggesting that storage duration alone may incompletely capture the metabolic state of stored red blood cell units.
editor: visual
editor_options:
  chunk_output_type: console

# Load libraries

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(broom.mixed) # for tidying up linear models 
library(emmeans)     # for the joint_tests() function
```

# Import 2,3_DPG dataset

```{r}
# Establish the file path
path <- here("data", "dpg_data.rds")
path
mydata <- readRDS(path)

glimpse(mydata)
head(mydata)
```

# Convert Day_3 to 3 into a new column (day_num = 3)

```{r}
library(dplyr)
mydata <- mydata |> 
  dplyr::mutate(day_num = readr::parse_number(day))|>
  dplyr::select(day_num, everything())
head(mydata)
```

# Pivot longer

```{r}
#| label: pivot-long
long_data<- mydata |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(day_num, day),
    names_to = "bag_id",
    values_to = "dpg_level"
  ) |> 
  filter(!is.na(dpg_level))
head(long_data)
```

# Export dataset for rechecking analysis

```{r}
write.csv(long_data, "long_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# Summarize by day

```{r}
#| label: descriptive-stats-dpg

library(psych)
desc_dpg <- psych::describeBy(long_data$dpg_level, group = long_data$day_num, mat = TRUE)
desc_dpg

```

# 4. Calculate Summary Statistics

```{r}
long_summary <- long_data |> 
  group_by(day_num) |> 
  summarize(
    N       = n(),
    Mean    = mean(dpg_level, na.rm = TRUE),   # Added na.rm = TRUE for safety
    Median  = median(dpg_level, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD      = sd(dpg_level, na.rm = TRUE),
    min     = min(dpg_level, na.rm = TRUE),
    max     = max(dpg_level, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |> 
  # 1. Explicitly sort by time step to guarantee row 1 is the true baseline
  arrange(day_num) |> 
  # 2. Calculate percentage relative to the true baseline day
  mutate(Pct_left = (Mean / first(Mean)) * 100)

print(long_summary)

```

# Check for normality

```{r}
day3_dpg <- long_data |> 
  filter(day_num == 3) |> 
  pull(dpg_level)

summary(day3_dpg)
hist(day3_dpg, main = "Day 3 DPG Levels", col = "lightblue")
qqnorm(day3_dpg)
qqline(day3_dpg, col = "red")
shapiro.test(day3_dpg)
```

# LMMs analysis for 2,3-DPG

```{r}
#| label: model1-dpg-lmm
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# LMM: 2,3-DPG ~ storage day with random intercept for pRBC unit

model1 <- lmer(dpg_level ~ day_num + (1 | bag_id), data = long_data, REML = TRUE)
summary(model1)

# Note: lmer() returns a singular fit (random intercept variance = 0),
# indicating no detectable between-bag baseline heterogeneity after
# accounting for the strong time trend. Cluster-robust SEs (CR2) via
# clubSandwich are reported to account for the repeated-measures structure.
robust_test <- clubSandwich::coef_test(
  model1,
  vcov       = "CR2",
  cluster    = long_data$bag_id,
  test       = "Satterthwaite"
)
robust_test
```

# Linear mixed models analysis for pH

```{r}
str(long_data_ph)
head(long_data_ph)
# Linear model
lin.model<- lm (formula = pH ~ day_num, data = long_data_ph)
summary(lin.model)
print(lin.model)
predicted <- predict(lin.model)

# Deconstruct lin.model
x <- as.numeric(long_data_ph$day_num)
y <- long_data_ph$pH

y.pred <- 7.0021 + x*(-0.0163)
SS.resid <- sum((y - y.pred)^2 )
SS.tot <- sum((y - mean(y))^2 )
r <- cor(x, y)
R.squared <- 1 - (SS.resid / SS.tot)
print(SS.tot)
print(SS.resid)
print(R.squared)
print( r^2 )

```

# Linear Mixed Model for pH

```{r}
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)
library(dplyr)

# Ensure correct ordering
long_data_ph <- long_data_ph |>
  arrange(day_num) |>
  mutate(day_num = factor(day_num, levels = unique(day_num)))

# Confirm dataset
long_data_ph |> count(day_num)

# Fit model
model_ph <- lmer(
  pH ~ day_num + (1 | bag_id),
  data = long_data_ph,
  REML = TRUE
)

summary(model_ph)

# Estimated marginal means
emm_ph <- emmeans(
  model_ph,
  ~ day_num,
  lmer.df = "satterthwaite"
)

summary(emm_ph)

# Contrasts vs Day 3
selected_contrasts <- contrast(
  emm_ph,
  method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
  ref = 1
)

summary(selected_contrasts, infer = TRUE)

# Singularity check
isSingular(model_ph)

```
